item.title: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star amazed by Bellingham after win vs Celta Vigo: ‘Best midfielder in the world’ After a season in which he appeared below his best level, Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham appears to have returned to his peak this campaign. One of the main objectives for manager Jose Mourinho when he took over the reins in the summer was to help the England international regain his mojo after a year disrupted by injuries, confusion over his role, and inconsistent displays. And, judging by how things have been going, it is safe to say that the 23-year-old is once again looking like one of the most influential players in the world. The latest display of his quality came on Saturday when he helped Real Madrid secure a 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu, scoring the equalising goal in the second half. Alvaro Benito left stunned by Bellingham Following the match, former Real Madrid player Alvaro Benito was effusive in praise of Bellingham, stating that the England star was enjoying his best moment at the club and was the best in the world in his position. Bellingham starred for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) “We are witnessing the best version of Bellingham. He has an influence on the game that he didn’t have before; now he’s a complete player,” Benito said on Cadena SER (h/t AS ). He also highlighted the mentality that separates Bellingham from other players, saying: “For me, he’s the best midfielder in the world; he’s capable of doing everything. Of all his virtues, the greatest is his ambition and his winning, competitive mentality. For me, without a doubt, this is Bellingham’s best moment at Real Madrid.” Vinicius and other teammates join in praise Bellingham, for his goal and overall contributions last night, was named the Man of the Match against Celta Vigo. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jude Bellingham (@judebellingham) Following the match, the Real Madrid superstar shared a post on Instagram, prompting several of his teammates to respond with messages of admiration. Vinicius Jr. wrote: “You’re the best,” while youngster Thiago Pitarch added: “Another level.” Real Madrid’s other hero against Celta Vigo, Carlos Espi, responded: “What a show.” Injured forward Rodrygo also joined in, writing: “What a player.” The result also saw Bellingham achieve a special milestone as he recorded his 100th La Liga victory with Real Madrid. Given his impact and influence, it does not come as a surprise to see Real Madrid working to extend Bellingham’s contract until 2032 .

item.title: Colorado’s 380-pound guard Chauncey Gooden took down more than a Cincinnati player defending a teammate
item.description: The Colorado Buffaloes saw their bowl hopes end Saturday with a 35-28 loss to the Cincinnati Bearcats at Nippert Stadium, and one of the afternoon’s most-shared clips belonged to a 380-pound offensive lineman. Late in the game, Cincinnati’s Antwan Peek Jr. stood over a Colorado receiver who was down after a play. As an official moved in to pull Peek away, Chauncey Gooden charged in and took down both Peek and the official. Players from both teams rushed in before officials separated them, and Deion Sanders stepped into the scrum to send his players away. Chauncey Gooden got his teammates back https://t.co/O9WFxWnIwC — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 21, 2026 Coach Prime Had To Get In Between Colorado Players And Cincinnati Players After The Game. Oh Boy… https://t.co/YNqyTHxPBD — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 21, 2026 Colorado had come to Ohio off a 42-32 upset of the then-No. 14 Houston Cougars, then turned the ball over four times on Saturday. Isaac Wilson threw three interceptions, and Cole Tabb scored four touchdowns as Cincinnati became bowl eligible and won in November for the first time since 2024 after 12 straight losses in the month. Travel problems the day before the game had put the Buffaloes behind before they arrived. Apr 11, 2026; Boulder, CO, USA; Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders before the start of the spring game at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images “Early in the game, we didn’t show up. We were still on the tarmac. Early turnovers crippled us,” Sanders said. He put the rest of the result on himself. “We just have no true consistency. We don’t know at this point how we’re going to show up. Is the offense going to show up, the defense going to show up, the special teams. All of it’s on me,” Sanders said . Who is Chauncey Gooden? Gooden is a second-year guard from Nashville who played at Lipscomb Academy and has started every game he has appeared in this season. After an Aug. 10 practice, assistant offensive line coach George Hegamin said there was “a lot more aggression and a lot more violence up front” and named Gooden as the lineman who brings that intent. A week before the trip to Cincinnati, Gooden was part of the line, with Xavier Payne, Sean Kinney, Leon Bell and Larry Johnson III, named the Big 12 Offensive Line of the Week after the Buffaloes ran 39 times for 249 yards and five touchdowns without allowing a sack in the win over Houston. Colorado managed 67 rushing yards in the first half and 121 for the game, and the loss dropped the Buffaloes to 4-7, guaranteeing a third losing season in Sanders’ four years in Boulder and a second straight year without a bowl. It was also Colorado’s 10th straight loss in Big 12 road games. In a season with little left to play for, Gooden’s most visible moment in Cincinnati came after a play was over, standing up for a teammate on the turf. item.title: Tennessee fans halt the game against LSU, reviving the 2021 scene with golf balls and mustard bottles at Lane Kiffin’s return
item.description: The Tennessee Volunteers beat the LSU Tigers 27-13 at Neyland Stadium on Saturday night, and with 3:14 left, the game stopped because of what came out of the stands. After a pass interference call gave LSU a first down at the Tennessee 30, fans threw golf balls, mustard bottles and other debris onto the field, and LSU’s players left their sideline until it was cleared. The objects were the same ones that rained down in October 2021, the last time Lane Kiffin brought a visiting team to Knoxville. His Ole Miss Rebels won 31-26 that night, Kiffin was hit by a golf ball, and University of Tennessee police reported 18 arrests and 47 ejections. The SEC fined Tennessee $250,000 , and the school banned 16 students and nine other fans from its athletic events. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin reacts to a play against the McNeese Cowboys during the second half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Kiffin, who coached Tennessee for one season in 2009, made his first trip back as LSU’s head coach. He was booed walking out for warmups, and a Chattanooga law firm flew a “Dolly Hated Kiffin” banner over the stadium before kickoff. Somebody decided to fly this banner over Neyland Stadium “Dolly hated Kiffin” Spicy in Knoxville https://t.co/jLKlqV9Nut — Trey Wallace (@TreyWallace) November 21, 2026 Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel had brought up the 2021 debris himself in July, when he was asked at SEC Media Days if the fan base had cooled on Kiffin. “I certainly hope that our fans haven’t cooled off. Whether it’s the grocery stores stocked up on mustard, or the sports stores that they’ve got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival,” Heupel said . Kiffin was asked after the game if the scene surprised him. “Probably not, when the coach says at SEC Media Days, ‘go buy your golf balls,'” Kiffin said . Fans threw golf balls and mustard bottles onto the field during LSU-Tennessee. https://t.co/3UBJvukeis — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 22, 2026 How much did the Neyland crowd actually affect LSU? LSU committed eight procedural penalties on offense, seven false starts and a delay of game, and ABC cameras caught quarterback Sam Leavitt on the sideline as center Braelin Moore told him it was too loud to hear anything on the field. Sep 12, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Tennessee Volunteers fans in the stands against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets in the second quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images “Their fans were elite. Been in a lot of stadiums, a lot of places. That was the loudest, most affected I’ve seen a team by a crowd. Credit to the crowd and credit to Tennessee for playing really well,” Kiffin said . Faizon Brandon ran for two fourth-quarter touchdowns as the Vols outscored LSU 14-0 in the period. item.title: Kirk Ferentz makes feelings on CFP committee clear after Iowa’s 34-17 win at Illinois
item.description: The Iowa Hawkeyes beat the Illinois Fighting Illini 34-17 in Champaign on Saturday to move to 9-2 without leading rusher Kamari Moulton, who is out for the season, taking control early and answering every time Illinois scored. Kirk Ferentz had barely left the field when Big Ten Network sideline reporter Brooke Fletcher asked what a win like that could show the College Football Playoff selection committee. Iowa came into the weekend at No. 15 in the committee’s rankings, the same spot it held a week earlier. A 28-7 win over the Purdue Boilermakers, Iowa’s third straight Big Ten win by a combined 82-17 , had left the Hawkeyes in place while the Oregon Ducks and Ohio State Buckeyes moved past them. Nov 11, 2023; Iowa City, Iowa, USA; Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz reacts during the fourth quarter against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at Kinnick Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care. Our goal is to come in here and win. It’s not easy winning in college football. It’s not easy on the road, conference game, so go right down the list, so I’m just really happy for our guys,” Ferentz told Fletcher. “I swear to God, I could care less about those guys. They’re gonna do what they want to do, and I really don’t care.” Iowa’s Kirk Ferentz on the CFP committee https://t.co/4LHs8zTIK4 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 21, 2026 Iowa beat Purdue by three touchdowns and held it to a single score, and the win did nothing for its ranking. The questions about style points followed the team to Illinois anyway. A committee that left a 28-7 Big Ten win unrewarded gives Ferentz little reason to chase margins now. Iowa’s two losses include a rivalry defeat that still shapes how its season is judged. The Minnesota Golden Gophers beat the Hawkeyes 13-10 on a field goal as time expired on Oct. 24, a game in which Iowa turned the ball over four times and changed quarterbacks, with Hank Brown replacing Jeremy Hecklinski in the second quarter. Iowa has won every game since. What can still move Iowa into the playoff field? No. 4 UCLA fell 18-16 in triple overtime at Michigan, the Indiana Hoosiers lost, and Ohio State, one of the two teams that jumped Iowa last week, fell 31-28 at Nebraska for its fourth loss of the season. Those results did more for Iowa than its own score. That Nebraska Cornhuskers team comes to Kinnick Stadium for Iowa’s regular-season finale on Friday, Nov. 27, at noon ET. A week ago, beating Nebraska would have looked like a routine rivalry win to close the season. It now means beating the team that just ended Ohio State’s playoff hopes, which gives Iowa’s resume something the committee can point to without Ferentz ever making the argument himself. item.title: What Bob Chesney told UCLA players in the locker room after triple-overtime loss to Michigan
item.description: Bob Chesney had gone 10 games at UCLA without addressing a losing locker room. That ended Saturday night at Michigan Stadium, where the Michigan Wolverines beat the No. 4 UCLA Bruins 18-16 in three overtimes and cost them a chance to clinch a spot in the Big Ten championship game. UCLA scored one touchdown all night, with 10 seconds left in regulation. Ty Dieffenbach threw an interception in the red zone in the first quarter and was strip-sacked while the Bruins were driving late in the first half. One of his two lost fumbles set up Michigan’s go-ahead touchdown early in the fourth quarter. In overtime, UCLA settled for two field goals before Madden Iamaleava’s two-point pass fell incomplete in the third period. Oct 17, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney in the first half against the Wisconsin Badgers at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short, and like we always say, we have to find a way to get better, period. That’s it, no excuses. I thought they played a really good game of football. We know they were tough. “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team, and you battled with that team, and then we came up a little short. “When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it,” Chesney said . Bob Chesney on UCLA’s loss at Michigan: “The message in the locker room was nobody hang your head. You played a really good team & you battled… When you have your opportunity, you’ve got to make the most of it against a really good defense like that. And we just didn’t do it.” https://t.co/3UDwFXMq1O — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 22, 2026 The 16 points were UCLA’s lowest total of the season. Chesney said afterward that the Bruins cannot give the ball away the way they did near the goal line, where the turnovers took points off the board. A defense that held Michigan to one touchdown in regulation gave UCLA enough to win. Who will play quarterback for UCLA against USC? The answer depends on Dieffenbach, who was carted off after a 6-yard run on the first play of overtime. Chesney had no update on the injury after the game. Dieffenbach had taken over as the starter after Nico Iamaleava’s season-ending knee injury in October, which leaves Madden Iamaleava, Nico’s younger brother, as the next option. “It’s tough to lose anybody. It’s the brand, the game that we play. We all understand that it’s really hard to make it through the whole season unscathed. Not the greatest moment to lose him. But at the same point, we have to trust Madden. He’s got to be able to deliver in those moments,” Chesney said . item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Hertha cruise to 4-0 derby victory over Cottbus Stefan Leitl’s side arrived at the LEAG Energie Stadion looking to build on their impressive 2-1 victory over promotion rivals Wolfsburg before the international break, and they made the perfect start to the Berlin-Brandenburg derby. The visitors needed just six minutes to break the deadlock, with Sebastian Grønning rising highest to head home Mads Pedersen’s corner from close range. Cottbus attempted to respond, with Justin Butler testing Marius Gersbeck from distance, while the hosts were briefly awarded a penalty in the 23rd minute after Deyovaisio Zeefuik appeared to handle inside the area. However, referee Florian Exner overturned his initial decision following a VAR review, ruling that the Hertha defender’s arm had been in a natural position. Energie thought they had found an equaliser shortly afterwards when Lucas Copado found the net following a set-piece, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Despite Cottbus showing some resistance, Hertha remained in control and almost doubled their advantage before the interval when Grønning was denied from close range by Marcel Lotka. The visitors did not have to wait long after the restart to extend their lead. Just three minutes into the second half, Jón Dagur Thorsteinsson flicked on a corner at the near post, allowing Paul Seguin to arrive unmarked and head home from close range. Cottbus’ hopes of mounting a comeback were dealt another significant blow in the 58th minute when Fousseny Doumbia was shown a straight red card for bringing down Thorsteinsson as the last defender. With a numerical advantage, Hertha were able to manage the remainder of the contest with relative comfort, Kevin Sessa came close to adding a third when his follow-up effort flew over the crossbar. The visitors eventually put the result beyond doubt in the closing stages, with Deyovaisio Zeefuik making it 3-0 in the 90th minute before substitute Gustaf Nilsson completed the scoring moments later. The Swedish forward’s strike was particularly memorable, marking his first goal for Hertha since joining the club. The emphatic victory means Hertha remain unbeaten after 12 league matches, having collected 34 points from a possible 36. They now hold a ten-point advantage over second-placed Nürnberg and are firmly establishing themselves as the early favourites for promotion. Cottbus, meanwhile, remain without a victory in their last seven league matches and sit 17th in the table with 11 points, continuing their difficult run since the start of the campaign.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Subtly Shots At Bam Adebayo After 50-Point Night
item.description: Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama secured a historic win on Saturday, Nov. 21, scoring 50 points while grabbing 18 rebounds, recording five blocks, and making four steals. The San Antonio Spurs star made history by becoming the first player since 1973 to hit those specific marks in one game. Per USA TODAY , he also became the first player in league history to score 50 points, block five shots, and make five 3-pointers in a single matchup. After the game, the young center made comments that have Heat fans talking. Wembanyama seemed to suggest his big night was natural and not the result of gamesmanship. He stated, “Unlike many of my peers, i’m not very good at statpadding.” All U Can Heat reported that Wembby did not name Bam Adebayo directly, but the context points toward the Miami center. The Stat Padding Debate Bam Adebayo scored 83 points in a March 2026 game that drew heavy criticism from the league. Some fans and players questioned whether the performance was real or if the rules were bent to help him reach the total but there was no credible discussions. Wembanyama’s comments about avoiding “stat padding” seem to address this exact controversy. This is not the first time Adebayo has faced questions about his effort or style. NBA Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett recently called Adebayo lazy on his podcast – a playful jab. Garnett said, “I don’t think he’s in great shape, I don’t think he’s running hard.” These previous criticisms make Wembanyama’s subtle jab hit harder for Miami supporters who know the context. A Rivalry Takes Shape Wembanyama is embracing a villain role that could be good for the NBA. Rivalries between players often make the league more entertaining for fans. With 14 wins in their last 15 games, the Spurs demonstrate they are a serious force in the Western Conference. All U Can Heat noted that while Wemby is in the West, his comments could spark a feud with Heat fans heading into their matchup later this year. The timing of these remarks adds fuel to the fire. Tyler Herro also scored a career-high 50 points for the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Yahoo Sports noted that the national hype might be on Herro’s former team, the Miami Heat, due to the release of “Grand Theft Auto 6.” Yet it was the Bucks guard who made fans pay attention with his own explosive scoring night. What Fans Should Watch It remains unclear if Wembanyama had one specific player in mind when he spoke. Since he never named Bam, the situation is more about reading between the lines. However, it would be shocking if Adebayo or any player with a recent breakout night did not take these words to heart. Player feuds function as well as team battles, making the NBA better when rivalries increase. For the Heat, Bam Adebayo currently averages 18.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists. item.title: “What the Unemployed Sound Like”: Landry Kiffin Gives Brutal Reply to Tennessee Crowd for Going After Dad Lane Kiffin
item.description: Sep 27, 2025; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin poses for a photo with his daughter Landry Kiffin prior to the game against the LSU Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. © Petre Thomas-Imagn Images It wasn’t a happy return to his old stomping grounds for Lane Kiffin as LSU was humbled 27-13 by Tennessee in Knoxville, and the fans’ hatred for their former head coach was visible as they created a raucous atmosphere inside Neyland stadium. Vols fans took over the game at multiple times, making their feelings about Kiffin known as they tossed objects onto the field, including golf balls, mustard bottles and other trash, and after the game, Lane Kiffin’s daughter Landry Kiffin’s support for her dad became public. Landry posted on social media platform TikTok about her experience with the fans, referring to them as “unemployed” as she walked around the stadium. “Rent free,” Landry captioned the video, as also posted by Jack Mac . “In case you’re wondering what the unemployed sound like,” she also wrote. Lane Kiffin Spoke About the Impact of the Crowd After the Game Lane Kiffin acknowledged that the crowd played a major role in his team being unable to get going against Tennessee. When asked about what LSU does in training to battle something like this, Kiffin explained his usual exercise. “I mean, we put the speakers right behind us and everything. And so again, we’ve been doing this for years and I just think that they somehow hit a level that’s louder. Plus, some players have louder claps. Quarterbacks over time,” Kiffin remarked in the postgame press conference. He further said he doesn’t feel it’ll be an issue going forward, but doesn’t want to motivate Arkansas, LSU’s next opponents. “I don’t think it’ll be an issue. I don’t want to motivate Arkansas, but I don’t think it’ll be an issue. They’re the same. Otherwise if you could redo it, you know, you’d look at different, you know, cadence from the offensive line.” The loss means LSU’s record stands at 6-5 now, and they need to pick up a win against Arkansas in the team’s next clash on Saturday. item.title: Sun Belt Week 12 Takeaways: Nearing the End
item.description: Photo credit: Marshall Athletics | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kate Pearson Halyburton, Editor With the 2026 college football regular season coming to an end, the Sun Belt Conference saw several teams effectively play for their seasons. Some games ended in blowouts, while one went down to the final seconds. Bowl eligibility and division leads were on the line. Let’s see how this week went for teams with a lot to play for. Sun Belt Week 12 Recap Georgia State at Marshall This matchup between Georgia State and Marshall was huge for both teams’ bowl eligibility aspirations. Let’s say both teams came to play, and this one went all the way down to the wire. The Thundering Herd ended up escaping with the victory over the Panthers, 28-27. Down seven with 10 seconds left, Ayden Pereira found Rodshaun Dorsey on a Hail Mary in the back of the end zone for the touchdown. Unfortunately for the Panthers, they missed the extra point to tie the game, leading to a tough loss. Quarterback Carlos Del Rio-Wilson started his first game for the Thundering Herd since Oct. 10. While he only completed 12 of 23 passes, he did throw three touchdowns and ran for an additional touchdown. The Thundering Herd gained bowl eligibility with this victory and head into next week’s game against Louisiana-Monroe with considerably less pressure. For the Panthers, there were some very good things that they showcased in this one, specifically on offense. Pereira had a much better showing than last week, and the run game was productive. The one mistake the Panthers would love to take back is the interception at the end of the first half by Pereira. While it didn’t lead to any points for the Thundering Herd, they were in field goal range and could have added three points; judging by the final score, those points would have been vital. This is a heartbreaking defeat for the Panthers, but all hope isn’t lost. They will return home and face a Louisiana team on a three-game winning streak. This game is absolutely a do-or-die game for the Panthers. A season that began with so much promise has come apart: five losses in their last six games, and now it hangs by a thread. item.title: “Weaponization of Caitlin Clark”: Former NBA Player Criticizes Online Backlash Around Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell
item.description: CHICAGO, IL – AUGUST 08: Kelsey Mitchell 0 of the Indiana Fever and Caitlin Clark 22 of the Indiana Fever during a game against the Chicago Sky on August 8, 2026 at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire WNBA, Basketball Damen, USA AUG 08 Indiana Fever at Chicago Sky EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon260808200 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Uncertainty regarding Kelsey Mitchell’s Indiana Fever future has blown up a multitude of conversations since the Fever’s first-round exit, and one of them has centered around the passionate fanbase of Caitlin Clark. In light of Mitchell’s free agency, former NBA player Etan Thomas has now questioned the very intent of the Fever superstar’s fanbase. “The Caitlin Clark Mob isn’t worried about supporting women’s basketball or even supporting the Indiana Fever,” Thomas wrote on X , posting a snippet of the interview he had on his YouTube podcast with American sportswriter David Zirin. “They’re committed to a continued weaponization of Caitlin Clark that treats every other talented woman on the roster like an inconvenience.” Thomas’ comments allude to the accounts given by former and current Indiana Fever players. In a 2024 exit interview, Aliyah Boston spoke about the harsh comments she received from the fans when she was playing badly. Mitchell also spoke about the difficulty of playing alongside Clark. “We got a lot of flak for just being on [Clark’s] team,” Mitchell said. The WNBA's biggest star is caught in a heated debate about respect and rivalry. Subscribe to stay informed on how this controversy reshapes women's basketball discourse. When Amber Cox, the Fever GM who was fired after the 2026 season, defended the Indiana Fever fanbase and said that the criticism against the Fever fanbase was baseless, former Fever player Brianna Turner called Cox’s statement “unequivocally false.” Zirin called out the Caitlin Clark fanbase for taking issue with things that were not even about the Fever as a team. “What makes things difficult for players like Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston is that they also get attacked by the Caitlin Clark Mob for taking her shots,” Zirin said on The Collision podcast. “Or for not standing up for her loudly enough. There’s this whole set of criticism where it’s not even about the team. It’s, why are you diminishing the Caitlin Clark Show by existing?” Mitchell has played nine seasons in the WNBA, all of them with the Fever. She has been their best scorer and one of the best in the league. However, it seems like a player who was once expected to end her career in Indiana might decide to leave for another team. “What I probably need and what’s probably best for me. So, I have to be selfish in that room,” she said about her free agency. One of the few reasons that the Fever should make re-signing Mitchell their top priority is because of the offense she brings to the team. She is one of the league’s most versatile scorers. item.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua #12 flexes after a play getting a first down during an NFL Wildcard football game against the Carolina Panthers, on Saturday, January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. item.title: The Yankees can ask more of Jonathan Loaisiga without asking for every big out
item.description: Jul 29, 2025; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees relief pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) reacts as he walks off the field after the top of the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jonathan Loaisiga went to Arizona and did the thing the Yankees spent years waiting to see: he took the ball for a full season. Mark Feinsand reported Friday for MLB.com that the right-hander agreed to return on a two-year deal worth about $18 million, with a club option for 2029. The report said the deal was pending a physical; the Yankees had not announced it. I’d make that deal, with one caveat. Let Loaisiga start clean innings. Don’t make the entire middle of the bullpen depend on his ability to work on short rest and escape somebody else’s trouble. Sep 23, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga (43) delivers a pitch in the ninth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What the Yankees would be paying for Loaisiga had a 2.42 ERA over 67 innings in 67 appearances for Arizona, according to his MLB record . He didn’t get there by blowing everybody away. Feinsand’s report put his strikeout rate at 18.4% and his walk rate at 5%. Baseball Savant’s contact profile shows why that combination worked: 55.8% ground balls and a 3.5% barrel rate. Those numbers matter in a clean seventh. Loaisiga can attack the first hitter instead of having to make a perfect pitch with a runner already in scoring position. If a hitter rolls over his sinker, he can get an out without getting deep into the count. He can also use a changeup off the sinker when a hitter is ready to swing at the harder pitch. It is a practical way to get three outs without trying to win every at-bat with a strikeout. The success wasn’t confined to one good month. Across his last 30 regular-season appearances he walked six in 32 2/3 innings. He also threw two scoreless innings against the Yankees on September 20. Those are two different snapshots from the same season, and neither tells you what his arm will do in April. They do help explain why I wouldn’t restrict him to one batter or reserve him for a save that may never come. One pitcher shouldn’t fill two openings New York non-tendered Fernando Cruz and Luis Gil . Getting Loaisiga back wouldn’t undo the Cruz decision, and it certainly wouldn’t replace Gil’s starts. The Yankees should still have an option for an inherited-runner spot where a strikeout is particularly valuable. The worst use of the reunion would be to buy a pitcher who can take charge of a whole inning and then expect him to put out every fire. The alternative is to use him as a traditional setup man if his availability proves steady and the other jobs are covered. I’d wait until the Yankees see how his arm responds to a normal spring schedule. He missed most of 2

item.title: Press Room | Comments after Juventus-Venezia
item.description: Press Room | Comments after Juventus-Venezia The Men’s First Team scored four second-half goals to beat Venezia 4-0 at the Allianz Stadium on Serie A Matchday 12. Head coach Luciano Spalletti and Teun Koopmeiners spoke to the press after the win on Sunday. LUCIANO SPALLETTI "We did well in terms of our mental strength, personality and character. The lads took control of the situation today, they did well. In the first half we weren’t quite up to scratch, we couldn’t find the time to close down their positions in defence, we were slow and stiff. In the second half, however, we did everything right. We pressed at the right moments, played through balls, and were more alert and fluid with our passing. "It was certainly crucial that the players recognised what was missing and then put it into practice on the pitch. [Nick] Woltemade is a technically gifted player; he needs to pick his own position and is good at linking up with his teammates. [Randal] Kolo Muani has the quality to do it all. He’s got pace, stamina and physicality. Koopmeiners doesn’t have that burst of speed in the middle of a match, but he has the ability to maintain a steady pace throughout the entire game. We’re pleased to have put him in a position where he can once again show what sort of player he is.” TEUN KOOPMEINERS “We played better in the second half; in the first half, we gave the ball away in some simple moments that we should have handled better. We can improve in terms of consistency. We need to control the game for the full 90 minutes. I feel good, I’m a midfielder, I’ve played plenty of matches in this area of the pitch and I’m now finding my rhythm here. I feel a great sense of responsibility when I play. I have experience from having played so many matches.”

item.title: Michigan State hockey responds after brawl to shut out No. 1 Michigan
item.description: EAST LANSING - Lansing State Journal sports reporter Nathaniel Bott breaks down No. 9 Michigan State hockey's 2-0 victory over No. 1 Michigan on Saturday, Nov. 21, at Munn Ice Arena. What happened MSU was looking to bounce back following a 5-1 defeat on the road in Ann Arbor on Friday, and the Spartans were able to get just enough offense while freshman goaltender Joshua Ravensbergen recorded his second career shutout, making 32 saves in a 2-0 MSU victory to earn a series split. Both sides were skating shorthanded after the Big Ten announced additional discipline from Friday night's third-period line brawl . MSU wound up dressing just five defensemen including sophomore Cole Ward, who made his season debut, after Patrick Geary, Sean Barnhill, and Matt Lahey were all suspended for two games. Meanwhile, a combination of suspensions and injuries left U-M with only seven healthy and eligible forwards. The Wolverines wound up dressing two reserve defensemen to skate on the wings of its makeshift third line, while third-string goaltender Julian Molinaro dressed as a forward, but did not see ice time. MSU started the scoring late in the first period when sophomore forward Anthony Romani roofed a rebound over U-M goaltender Jack Ivankovic with just 10 seconds remaining to put the Spartans up 1-0. The teams skated to a scoreless second, and then in the third period, MSU got a much-needed insurance goal while on the man advantage. Freshman forward Mason West, who normally doesn't see time on the power play, took a pass from sophomore forward Eric Nilson and sniped a shot under Ivankovic's glove to give MSU a two-goal cushion. What it means This was a game MSU needed badly, facing a U-M team that was effectively only rolling out two forward lines from the jump,. While there were still dangerous players and chances for the Wolverines, MSU was effective defensively with just five blue-liners, and Ravensbergen was excellent in net. As the game continued, U-M's legs started to wear down. MSU was responsible with their shift lengths, especially with its defensemen, and when the Wolverines attempted to generate any offense in the third period, it fizzled quickly. Ivankovic and Ravensbergen were both terrific in net, with U-M's sophomore netminder making a few outstanding saves to keep MSU off the scoreboard. MSU was also missing first-line center Cayden Lindstrom, who was out for an undisclosed reason. Forwards Cole Burke and Griffin Jurecki also made their season debuts, with Jurecki providing some juice on the fourth line and Burke hitting the crossbar with a shot once in the third period. What they said MSU coach Adam Nightingale, on the game overall: "That was an awesome response from our group, and obviously both teams came in missing some guys from suspension, but I thought we got to our game right off the bat. I thought we played how we needed to play. At the end of the day, the best thing we can help our kids and players to develop is how to be a winner,

item.title: Blackburn rally without Tony Mowbray to deny Burnley long-awaited home win
item.description: Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues . In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted. Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season. Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message ‘We’re with you, Tony’ on the back and the number 900 on the front. Blackburn honoured Tony Mowbray before kick-off (PA) Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute. Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead. The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react. But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a T-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras. Andri Gudjohnsen paid tribute to Mowbray while celebrating his equaliser (PA) Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off. The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio. Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2. Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

item.title: Maple Leafs 2027 1st Rounder Continues to Rise; It’s Time for the League to Step In and Decide: Flyers or Bruins?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For all intents and purposes, the Toronto Maple Leafs traded the same first-round draft pick twice at the 2025 NHL Trade Deadline. Two trade deadlines ago, the Maple Leafs were in the hunt and were wheeling and dealing, trying to push their roster over the edge for a run at the Stanley Cup. It started by trading their 2027 First-round pick, top-10 protected, to the Philadelphia Flyers, alongside Nikita Grebenkin , in exchange for center Scott Laughton . Then, as a buzzer-beater at the deadline, they traded their 2026 first-rounder, top-5 protected, along with prospect Fraser Minten , to the Boston Bruins for defenseman Brandon Carlo. At the time, everything seemed fine. But the 2026 NHL Draft Lottery has sent the league into a bit of a spiral. The Maple Leafs won the lottery, selecting 1st overall in the 2026 NHL Draft, which fell under protection. The problem? Both the Flyers and Bruins feel entitled to the Leafs 2027 first-rounder, which currently has the 4th-best odds at the top pick. If the Leafs’ pick somehow falls outside of the top-10, it becomes easy: the Flyers receive that pick. However, if it falls inside of the protection, then things can get murky. Should the Flyers be entitled to the pick since their trade was completed first? Or should the Bruins receive the 2027 pick because they received the earlier 2026 draft pick? Before the 2026 NHL Draft Lottery, we wrote what our friends at Puckpedia had reported : if the Leafs’ 2026 pick is protected, then they would have to choose who receives the 2027 pick if it’s inside the top 10. On Sportsnet’s Saturday night headlines , NHL insider Elliotte Friedman shared the same thing. “If it is in the top 10, as it stands now, Toronto chooses which team gets it, and the other team would get the unprotected 2028 first.” “We’ve been trying to get some clarity from the league,” Friedman added. “Does this stand? Is this the way it’s actually going to go? And the answer is yes. In the eyes of the NHL, the way that the trade information is put together, it’s quite clear that it’s Toronto’s choice. So the Maple Leafs do have the option of which team to pick.” That is going to create a tricky scenario to navigate for the Flyers and the Bruins. It’s time for the league to step in. The NHL Needs to Step in and Force a Decision, Sooner Rather than Later On Saturday night headlines, Friedman brought up the possibility of the Maple Leafs trying to squeeze some extra value for their draft pick. “Can [The Maple Leafs] go to the Bruins and the Flyers and say, ‘Do you want one of these two, and what are you willing to consider for us to pick you?'” Now, that sounds like it’s extortion. To a degree, it is. But Friedman says that it’s possible. “It’d have to be part of a bona fide trade. If it’s an actual bona fide trade that one of those two would make with the Maple Leafs involving other pieces, then yes, that could happen. The league still has to approve any deal, but Toronto can

item.title: Bayern's Musiala suffered another seizure this week
item.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala returned for the first time in two months on Friday (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Bayern Munich and Germany midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered another previously undisclosed seizure this week, according to information received by AFP subsidiary SID on Sunday. The incident, which is categorised by a brief and temporary loss of consciousness or awareness, occurred at training on Monday. Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a "neurological disorder" which can lead to "temporary but treatable seizures". Monday's incident was the second since Musiala's announcement, with the player reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play. News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers' union FIFPRO for a "coordinated campaign" to pressure the Germany international to renegotiate his 2025-extended contract. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives," FIFPRO said in a statement. On Friday, Bayern supervisory board member and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the midfielder may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form. "Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium," Rummenigge said. "If he doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency -- because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable." sid-dwi/ea

item.title: ‘Are you loyal to the team or Pat (Cummins)?’: Steve O'Keefe slams Josh Hazlewood for repeating AUS captain's Sandpapergate defence
item.description: ‘Are you loyal to the team or Pat (Cummins)?’: Steve O'Keefe slams Josh Hazlewood for repeating AUS captain's Sandpapergate defence originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Steve O'Keefe has hit out at Australia pacer Josh Hazlewood's defence of his captain, Pat Cummins. Hazlewood's comments about threatening to walk away from Test cricket did not sit well with O'Keefe. A plea for empathy towards Cameron Bancroft forms the core of the criticism. MORE: Boycott feels Smith and Warner should've served longer bans in 'Sandpapergate' Josh Hazlewood criticized for backing Pat Cummins after Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelations Steve O'Keefe has slammed Josh Hazlewood and went on to ask whether the fast bowler's loyalty lies with the Australian team or with captain Pat Cummins. The former Test spinner was in no mood to soften his stance during his appearance on the Chin Music podcast. The row stemmed from a chain of events that began when Usman Khawaja released his autobiography, Sabr. In it, he claimed that everyone in the 2018 Cape Town squad knew about the ball-tampering plan, a statement that drew an instant and angry response from several of his former teammates. Cummins responded with a 68-minute press conference in Sydney, where he called the claims "complete and utter nonsense" and denied having any knowledge of the plot. Cricket Australia then announced an independent forum in which the 2018 tourists could give their accounts in private, and Cameron Bancroft published a 4,000-word statement of his own. Hazlewood joined the debate on Saturday, November 21, with an interview that backed his captain strongly. The pacer was speaking publicly for the first time since the controversy flared up again. He has spent the last fortnight training with Cummins in Sydney in preparation for Australia's four-Test home series against New Zealand, which begins on December 9 in Perth. MORE: ‘Booed and cheered’: Khawaja gets mixed reception at T20 Gold Cup "It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days from different people," Hazlewood said. "I want to back Pat and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain." The fast bowler said he agreed 100 per cent with Cummins' Sydney press conference. He also denied being an architect of the 2018 plan and reiterated that he did not know a foreign substance had been used on the ball in South Africa. He said: "To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that [sandpaper] is never going to happen again - I think is just a remarkable job. He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response." Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Nebraska football team brought down the Ohio State Buckeyes, 31-28, on Saturday. It was a massive win for the Cornhuskers, who have gotten their season back on track after a four-game losing streak. Fans stormed the field as the final whistle blew to celebrate the Cornhuskers’ first win over a ranked opponent since 2016. One fan got a bit too enthusiastic about the win, though. After the game, he was spotted walking out with a row of bleachers with him . A Nebraska fan appeared to bring home a row of bleachers with him after the Ohio State win. pic.twitter.com/VipZp3INl2 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 21, 2026 It’s still a mystery how the fan managed to leave Memorial Stadium and evade nearby security while carrying quite a large part of it. Whatever he did, it worked like a charm. But it remains to be seen whether he will be able to hold onto the bleachers if school officials decide they want it back. Senior quarterback Anthony Colandrea had a huge game for Nebraska. He finished 19-of-28 for 200 yards with three passing touchdowns, as well as 63 yards and a rushing score to lead the Cornhuskers. The win helped ease the pressure on Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule, who had been feeling the pressure after their recent losing skid. Rhule fired his offensive coordinator after their 24-13 loss to Illinois, and that decision seems to have sparked his team. The Cornhuskers have scored 31 points in each of their two games since the move after failing to reach 20 points during their four-game losing streak. Rhule and Nebraska will look to end the regular season on a high note on Friday when they visit the Iowa Hawkeyes. item.title: Northern Ireland complete series win over Gibraltar
item.description: Northern Ireland were comfortable winners in both matches with Gibraltar [Getty Images] Northern Ireland Warriors beat Gibraltar Campions 71-30 to complete a Test double in Antrim. After a 74-29 victory on Saturday, Northern Ireland had too much for Gibraltar again and secured the series in their first home matches in three years. With an attack led by the impressive Lisa Bowman, the hosts held a 19-8 lead after the first quarter and had extended their lead to 22 points at half-time. Northern Ireland continued to pull clear and led by 54-21 by the end of the third quarter, and debutant Anna Rice scored the final point of the game as the hosts ran out comfortable winners. The series has acted as preparation for the 2027 World Cup in Australia, which will take place in Sydney from 25 August until 5 September. "I think it was a great performance. We got every player on the court but I'm just really pleased to see the consistency across four quarters," Northern Ireland head coach Sheonah Forbes told BBC Sport NI. "It's just a little comma in our journey, it's definitely not a full stop. We'll regroup in January, put our foot down and build nicely through the months to come." Northern Ireland captain Michelle Magee said the two matches with Gibraltar made the squad feel "really connected". "Gibraltar came out strong and we want experiences like that. We don't want anything handed to us," Magee said. "Everyone wants to get on that plane to Sydney at the end of the year and it's really healthy. We're a competitive group, and any time you come into a Warriors camp you have to be at your best." Northern Ireland seal comfortable win over Gibraltar A men's netball World Cup - not a question of if, but when?

item.title: Massimiliano Allegri insists ‘extraordinary’ Kevin De Bruyne is fully committed to Napoli amid PSV transfer talk
item.description: SSC Napoli v FK Bodo/Glimt - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri has lavished praise on Kevin De Bruyne, labelling the veteran midfielder as "extraordinary" despite persistent rumours linking him with a move away from the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. The Belgian playmaker has been the subject of intense speculation regarding a potential switch to PSV Eindhoven during the upcoming January transfer window. Allegri dismisses exit talk Allegri has moved to quieten the noise surrounding De Bruyne’s future at Napoli , following a narrow 1-0 win against Torino in Serie A. Despite reports suggesting a potential move to the Eredivisie , the Italian tactician was adamant that the midfielder remains a vital part of his project in Naples. Allegri was quick to shut down suggestions that the Belgian has his eyes on the exit door as the winter market approaches. "There is no foot inside and one foot outside, he is an extraordinary player. Just look at tonight, he is doing well," the Napoli boss told DAZN , as quoted by TUTTOmercatoWEB . Last year he was out for four or five months with an injury, he's not a kid. He did well for the national team, but he also did well with us. Sometimes perception makes you give a different opinion, I'm very happy with him as with the others." Tactical rest for weary De Bruynee De Bruyne's inclusion on the bench for the clash with Torino marked the fifth time he has started as a substitute in domestic competition this season. Allegri explained that this was a tactical necessity given the dense fixture list and the player's recent involvement with the Belgian national team. The decision appears to be a calculated move to keep the playmaker fresh for crucial upcoming fixtures. "It is not a matter of management, but that he has played many games, he played for the national team, tonight the changes will be important, he is a player of the highest technical quality, he has improved a lot in his physical condition and he came from a long period of inactivity. We are very happy with him," Allegri clarified. Managing the Napoli pressure cook The narrow victory over Torino was characterized by resilience and defensive solidity, qualities that Allegri felt had been missing in recent outings. He acknowledged the atmospheric pressure in Naples but urged for calm as the team looks to climb the Serie A standings. The coach noted that the squad finally showed the necessary "positive energy" to grind out a result against a difficult opponent. "I think the boys have taken note of the reality of Napoli's current moment, football is made of results. Today we had one point more than Torino, in these ten games we lacked the fear of conceding a goal, that extra centimeter that gives you the possibility of bringing home victories," Allegri remarked. item.title: Watford sack Alessio Dionisi after Sheffield United thrashing as managerial merry-go-round continues
item.description: Watford have sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday’s 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United, with the Hornets beginning the search for yet another manager at Vicarage Road. The Italian departs after just five months in charge, having overseen 18 matches since his appointment in June. Dionisi initially made an encouraging impression, guiding Watford to an opening-day victory over Southampton before picking up respectable draws against West Ham United and Wrexham. However, results have deteriorated significantly since that promising start, with the Hornets managing just three wins in their last 13 matches. For exclusive stories and all the detailed EFL news you need, subscribe to The Football League Paper website, digital edition, or newspaper from as little as 14p a day. Search begins Saturday’s comprehensive defeat at Bramall Lane proved the final straw, leaving Watford 21st in the Championship table – four points clear of the relegation zone. The club confirmed Dionisi’s departure in a statement on Sunday, also announcing that assistants Fabio Spighi, Luca Vigiani and Dan Thomassen had left. Sporting director Luke Dowling said: “We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts. “As I’m sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future. “The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly.” THE END OF THE ROAD: Alessio Dionisi has left his role as Watford head coach after five months in charge. PICTURE: Alamy Familiar story Dionisi becomes the latest casualty of the managerial instability that has become a familiar feature of life at Vicarage Road under the Pozzo family. Since Tom Cleverley’s departure at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, Watford have appointed Paulo Pezzolano, Javi Gracia, Ed Still and Dionisi, with Charlie Daniels also taking temporary charge for two matches. Dionisi was the club’s 12th head coach since the end of the 2020-21 season and the 24th managerial appointment since the Pozzo family took ownership in 2012, excluding interim appointments. Only Gracia, during his second spell at the club, managed more than 20 games among the four permanent appointments since Cleverley’s departure. The latest change also comes against a backdrop of growing frustration among supporters over the club’s direction, with former owner Sir Elton John and ex-Watford striker Troy Deeney among those to have voiced their concerns this season. With the Championship campaign approaching a busy period, Hornets fans will hope the club’s next appointment can deliver a more consistent run of results and endure a longer stint at the helm. item.title: Ilia Topuria blames shoulder injury for brother Aleksandre’s UFC Qatar loss, tells critics where to shove it
item.description: DOHA, QATAR - NOVEMBER 21: Aleksandre Topuria of Georgia prepares to face Santiago Luna of Mexico in a bantamweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at ABHA Arena on November 21, 2026 in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) The Topuria brothers have suffered another loss, this time with Aleksandre Topuria losing to Santiago Luna via split decision on the undercard of UFC Qatar. The elder Topuria brother was throwing hard shots that were hurting Luna, but Luna put twice the pace on his opponent, earning a squeaker of a decision via 30–27, 29–28 and 28-29 scores. You can question the judges’ scoring on this one (we certainly did), and now we’re learning that Aleksandre injured his shoulder just 40 seconds into the fight. That’s according to his little brother and former UFC featherweight and lightweight champion Ilia Topuria, who wrote a lengthy statement following the defeat. A close contest ⚔️ Santiago Luna wins the battle against Aleksandre Topuria by split decision! [ #UFCQatar | LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/0pAoPSuHLH — UFC (@ufc) November 21, 2026 “In the opening minutes of the fight, my brother dislocated his left shoulder, an injury that completely changed the course of the fight,” Topuria wrote on X (formerly Twitter). “Many of you were probably wondering what was happening, why he wasn’t throwing combinations, why he wasn’t going for takedowns, or why he kept moving backward.” “The answer is simple: we weren’t seeing the Aleks we all know. We were watching a warrior trying to compete with a dislocated shoulder, unable to use his weapons, unable to keep his guard up the way he normally does, and forced to fight a completely different fight from the one he had prepared for. And even under those circumstances, he took the fight to a split decision. To me, that says far more about him than any result ever could.” Topuria then went on to attack the haters and doubters who have once again piled on following a family loss. “To those who take pleasure in other people’s defeats and use every opportunity to spit out their frustration, let me tell you something: focus on building your own lives,” he wrote. “The envy, bitterness, and hatred you project onto others say nothing about us. They reveal everything about the world you carry inside yourselves.” Yesterday, we added another valuable experience to our journey. As I always say, glory and pain walk hand in hand. In the opening minutes of the fight, my brother dislocated his left shoulder, an injury that completely changed the course of the fight. Many of you were probably… pic.twitter.com/G6sAtlQs2J — Ilia Topuria (@Topuriailia) November 22, 2026 “For years, plenty of people have tried to take advantage of us. And instead of showing even the slightest gratitude for what we’ve done for them, some have chosen to spread bullshit and talk shit about us behind our backs. And if you’re reading this wondering whether I’m talking about you, then I probably am. F–k you.” T

item.title: Tottenham stun Man City to end 17-match winning WSL run
item.description: Manchester City ’s long winning home run in the Women’s Super League came to an end as they were stunned by Tottenham. Khadija Shaw put City ahead with only 10 minutes gone but Cathinka Tandberg levelled late in the first half and goals from Matilda Vinberg and Jess Naz secured a 3-1 victory for the visitors. City had been on a 17-match winning run at home in the WSL , with their last defeat coming back in March 2025 against Chelsea. Tottenham players celebrate at the final whistle after overcoming Man City (PA) The result means City stay two points behind leaders Chelsea, while Tottenham are now only five points further back in fifth. Spurs remain a point adrift of Manchester United , who left it very late to claim a 2-1 victory over Birmingham . Lee Geum-min put struggling Birmingham in front in only the fourth minute and United struggled to create clear-cut chances, while Phallon Tullis-Joyce made a couple of crucial saves. Man United scored two late goals to earn victory at Birmingham (PA) The visitors finally found the breakthrough 10 minutes from time through Elisabeth Terland, and Simi Awujo broke Birmingham hearts with a header four minutes into added time.

item.title: Insider Shares Garrett Wilson Warning Hours Before Jets Chargers Game
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: Garrett Wilson #5 of the New York Jets warms up before a game against the Buffalo Bills at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty The New York Jets are in the middle of another terrible season at 2-8 through the first 10 games. There is a strong possibility that it could get worse as the losses continue to pile up. ESPN’s Rich Cimini warned that it could cause star wide receiver Garrett Wilson to demand a trade. “Embattled coach Aaron Glenn needs a few wins desperately. The locker room needs wins, too. A two- or three-win season might be just enough to push Garrett Wilson over the edge; the star receiver already has stated that he prioritizes winning over all else,” Cimini described. “There are benefits to winning some games. If the Jets go 2-15, Garrett Wilson could say at the end of the year, ‘I’m out of here, guys. This is a lost cause.’ So there is some benefit to winning football games. It may not benefit Aaron Glenn, may not save his job, but I think it’s good for the morale of the team, and I think there is always positives to winning,” Cimini explained on the “Jets Collective” podcast this week. Careful What You Wish For The Jets’ playoff hopes are on life support at 2-8. They haven’t been mathematically eliminated yet, but that feels like a game of when, not if. With that path not being very realistic, a large section of Jets fans would prefer their team lose to increase their position in the 2027 NFL Draft. Over the next two weeks, the Jets will hit the road to play the Los Angeles Chargers and the Miami Dolphins , respectively. If the NFL Draft started today, the Chargers would hold the No. 2 overall pick and the Dolphins would hold the No. 3 overall pick, per Tankathon . So if the Jets lost to both of those teams, they would be leapfrogged in the draft order, which would be good news, but according to Cimini, that could have dire consequences. “If the Jets (2-8) beat the Chargers this Sunday at SoFi Stadium, their chances of landing the top pick would drop from 6% to 1%, according to ESPN Analytics. Their chances would jump to 8% with what would be their sixth straight loss,” Cimini shared. Beauty Is in the Eye of the Beholder Cimini said he might feel slightly differently about his anti-tanking take if there was a clear-cut blue-chip prospect in this class like a Peyton Manning or an Andrew Luck, etc. However, he doesn’t feel like this draft has that kind of player at the quarterback position. So why be in a rush to get the top pick when the consolation prize wherever you end up picking might just be as good? ESPN New York’s Jake Asman recently lamented that the Jets haven’t held the No. 1 overall pick amid all of their losing: “The craziest part about the Jets having the longest playoff drought in North American sports is that they haven’t picked No. 1 overall ONCE during this entire stretch of ineptitude. item.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview)
item.description: null " Star Trek: First Contact " celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"? We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile! "What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. ILM’s John Knoll, the guy who won the Oscar for 'Star Wars,' just happened to be our Special Effects Supervisor." "Star Trek: First Contact" celebrates its 30th birthday on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: Paramount) "First Contact" is filled with memorable moments and indelible performances, some of which certainly stand out for Frakes looking back over the years on the production. "The two things that always come to mind were the beautiful scene with Alfre [Woodard] and Patrick, the Moby Dick scene, where she says, 'You broke your little ships,'" he recalls. "I was sitting under the camera with my face in my hands, watching two heavyweights go at it take after take. It was what you dream of. They were into it. The writing was great. We had time to do it right, and they were fabulous together. "That and the Cromwell and Marina drunk on tequila scene. It's not only one extended take, but it contributes to the pace of the movie in the right kind of way. My wife tells me that I was really good in that scene because I was exhausted and relaxed. It’s true, you’re exhausted when you’re filming and acting at the same time. I got to sit ther

item.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
item.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. item.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. item.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
item.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. item.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
item.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts. The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it. She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added. Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation.
